identity.name: Compute Activity in a Dormant Cloud Region (Cryptomining) — CDR (SIM-CDR-024)
identity.summary: Stolen AWS credentials launch EC2 compute in a never-used region, then burst large GPU instances to mine cryptocurrency. SIM-CDR-024 drives cloud_storage_compute_emitter to emit CloudTrail RunInstances into cloud_audit_logs, firing two XSIAM alerts: 'Compute activity in dormant cloud region' (T1535) and 'Suspicious heavy allocation of compute resources - possible mining activity' (T1496).
identity.description: Detection-validation card for the XSIAM Cloud Storage & Compute analytics alerts 'Compute activity in dormant cloud region' (T1535) and 'Suspicious heavy allocation of compute resources - possible mining activity' (T1496), both keyed on the cloud_audit_logs dataset. The dormant-region alert is an Analytics detection anchored on a per-account region-usage baseline (a region dormant for >90 days that suddenly launches instances is anomalous); the heavy-allocation alert is an auto-tuned behavioral-ML (ABIOC) detection anchored on a learned per-principal compute-allocation baseline (a burst of GPU/high-core instance types reads as a mining fleet). The scenario SIM-CDR-024 emits the driving telemetry via the cloud_storage_compute_emitter EAL plugin and includes a validation XQL that confirms the emitted RunInstances records landed in cloud_audit_logs, plus a correlation rule that stitches the dormant-region landing and the mining-shaped heavy allocation into one cloud cryptomining incident.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-024 — driven by the cloud_storage_compute_emitter analytics log-streamer EAL plugin (dormant_region_activity + heavy_compute_allocation presets against the cloud_audit_logs dataset).

prerequisites.description: An operator-supplied HTTP log collector (XSIAM Broker VM HTTP applet / Cribl / nginx forwarder) already wired into Cortex XSIAM as the cloud_audit_logs (CloudTrail) source, reachable from the CortexSim beacon host and on the campaign target_allowlist.

payload.code:
# Drive the cloud_storage_compute_emitter analytics log-streamer to POST
# shape-true CloudTrail RunInstances records into the operator's collector.
# No real AWS tenant is touched and no instance is launched — every record is a
# synthetic JSON blob shaped like the cloud_audit_logs (CloudTrail) schema.
set -euo pipefail
: "${COLLECTOR_URL:=https://collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid/cloud/events}"
: "${COLLECTOR_HOST:=collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid}"
cat > /tmp/sim-cdr-024.yml <<YML
campaign_id: CMP-CDR-024
name: "CDR — dormant-region compute then mining-shaped heavy allocation"
authorized_by: "domain-consultant@paloaltonetworks.com"
simulation_authorized: true
target_allowlist:
  - "$COLLECTOR_HOST"
dry_run: false
steps:
  - step_id: dormant-region
    plugin: cloud_storage_compute_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "$COLLECTOR_URL"
      provider: aws
      event_pattern: dormant_region_activity
      iterations: 1
  - step_id: heavy-allocation
    plugin: cloud_storage_compute_emitter
    params:
      collector_url: "$COLLECTOR_URL"
      provider: aws
      event_pattern: heavy_compute_allocation
      iterations: 1
      burst_count: 10
YML
python3 -m scripts.eal_simulator.cli run /tmp/sim-cdr-024.yml --live

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Full URL of the operator's HTTP log collector fronting the XSIAM cloud_audit_logs ingestion door.

expected_artifacts.description: Synthetic CloudTrail RunInstances records (eventSource ec2.amazonaws.com) in a dormant region and a GPU-instance burst, POSTed to the collector and normalised into the cloud_audit_logs dataset.

abiocs.name: Suspicious Heavy Allocation of Compute Resources - Possible Mining Activity
abiocs.description: ABIOC (is_ml=true) — the XSIAM Cloud Storage & Compute analytics alert 'Suspicious heavy allocation of compute resources - possible mining activity'. Auto-tuned behavioral-ML anchored on a learned per-principal compute-allocation baseline: a short-window burst of large GPU / high-core instance types (a mining-shaped fleet) far above the principal's normal allocation profile.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter eventSource = "ec2.amazonaws.com" and eventName = "RunInstances"
| filter instance_type in ("p4d.24xlarge", "p5.48xlarge", "g5.48xlarge", "g6e.48xlarge")
| comp count() as gpu_launches, sum(instances_requested) as total_requested by userIdentity.arn, awsRegion
| filter gpu_launches >= 3 or total_requested >= 20
| fields userIdentity.arn, awsRegion, gpu_launches, total_requested
abiocs.causality_anchor: Per-principal compute-allocation baseline: the ML model learns each principal's normal instance-type mix and volume; a burst of GPU/high-core types with an outsized requested count anchors the mining-shaped deviation.

xql_queries.name: Compute Activity in Dormant Cloud Region
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter eventSource = "ec2.amazonaws.com" and eventName = "RunInstances"
| filter region_dormant_days > 90
| comp count() as instances_launched by userIdentity.arn, awsRegion, recipientAccountId
| filter instances_launched >= 1
| fields userIdentity.arn, awsRegion, recipientAccountId, instances_launched

xql_queries.name: Dormant-Region and Heavy-Allocation RunInstances Landing Check
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter eventName = "RunInstances" and eventSource = "ec2.amazonaws.com"
| filter dormant_region_marker = true or heavy_compute_allocation_marker = true
| comp count() as observed_records by awsRegion, instance_type
| sort desc observed_records
| fields awsRegion, instance_type, observed_records

correlation_rules.name: Dormant-Region Compute Escalating to Mining-Shaped Heavy Allocation
correlation_rules.logic: Fires when analytics `Compute Activity in Dormant Cloud Region` and abioc `Suspicious Heavy Allocation of Compute Resources - Possible Mining Activity` both observe RunInstances activity for the same recipientAccountId and userIdentity.arn within a 30-minute window — stitching the dormant-region landing and the mining-shaped GPU burst into ONE cloud cryptomining incident rather than two isolated alerts.

products.evidence_query: dataset = cloud_audit_logs | filter eventName = "RunInstances" and eventSource = "ec2.amazonaws.com" | comp count() as launches by userIdentity.arn, awsRegion, instance_type | sort desc launches

threat_scenarios.name: Cloud cryptomining — dormant-region compute + mining-shaped heavy allocation
threat_scenarios.description: Validate that Cortex XSIAM raises the two Cloud Storage & Compute ML analytics alerts when an adversary stands up compute in a never-used region and bursts a fleet of large GPU instances, and that the correlation engine stitches them into a single cryptomining incident.

threat_steps.objective: The 'Compute activity in dormant cloud region' Analytics alert fires when the streamer emits a RunInstances record in a region dormant for the baseline window.
preconditions: cloud_audit_logs (CloudTrail) source wired into XSIAM with the ML analytics content enabled.
Operator collector reachable and on the campaign target_allowlist.
steps: Observe the dormant-region Analytics alert raise an alert.
success_criteria: Analytics `Compute Activity in Dormant Cloud Region` raises one alert for the canary account.

threat_steps.objective: The 'Suspicious heavy allocation of compute resources' ABIOC fires on the GPU-instance burst and the correlation stitches the dormant-region Analytics alert and the heavy-allocation ABIOC into one incident.
preconditions: TC-CDR-024A telemetry present in the run window.
steps: Run SIM-CDR-024 step-02 (cloud_storage_compute_emitter, heavy_compute_allocation preset, burst_count 10).
Run the validation XQL to confirm the RunInstances records landed.
Observe the heavy-allocation ABIOC and the CR-CDR-0024 correlation fire.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Suspicious Heavy Allocation of Compute Resources - Possible Mining Activity` raises one alert.
Correlation `CR-CDR-0024` raises one cryptomining incident stitching the dormant-region Analytics alert and the heavy-allocation ABIOC.

preventive_controls: Deny-list or SCP-restrict AWS regions the organisation does not operate in so RunInstances in a dormant region fails at the control plane.
Enforce service-control-policy quotas on GPU / high-core instance families and require an approval workflow for large-fleet allocation.
Scope IAM so no single credential can launch compute across all regions; require MFA for EC2 RunInstances in production accounts.
detection_engineering: Enable the Cortex XSIAM Cloud Storage & Compute analytics content on the cloud_audit_logs dataset (the dormant-region alert is an Analytics detection; the heavy-allocation alert is an auto-tuned ABIOC).
Correlate the dormant-region landing with the mining-shaped heavy allocation on the shared account/principal so the SOC sees one cryptomining incident rather than two isolated alerts.
Baseline each account's region-usage and per-principal instance-type/volume profile so the ML deviations stay tight; re-tune after legitimate new-region expansions.
